text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- To encourage the growth of production is a national imperative need, George Paunescu, President of Romanian employers' association, says in an interview.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- After Romania's first nuclear reactor at Cernavoda had gone on stream, trade union sources said the other reactors should be pulled down as they have deteriorated in time.
ADEVARUL

- The November polls will be the start of economic nightmare. Owing to rising spending and subsidies, the state budget gap will account for some 3.5 percent of the gross domestic product, the newspaper says.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Petrom RA 's Fortuna offshore drilling rig has set off to the Marmara for drilling works there under a contract with Turkey's national oil company.
AZI
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will give a loan to a Romanian brewer to produce Tuborg beer.
LIBERTATEA

- Romania's energy programme for the period spanning April 1996-March 1997 provides for crude oil imports of some 9.0 million tonnes. The government has guaranteed a $200 million loan for these imports.
- Romania will import sugar beet for processing in local factories to cover the sugar deficit expected for this year.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The newspaper publishes two opinion polls taken by two different institutes. One of them shows President Ion Iliescu, presidential candidate of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), leading by 33 percent his rival Emil Constantinescu of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR). Constantinescu is at head with 32 percent in the other.
- Bucharest hosts an international festival of Yiddish- language theatre.
ADEVARUL
- The editorial analyses the health system as outlined in the electoral programmes of the main political parties ahead of the November 3 presidential and parliamentary elections.

- The presidential candidates of the main three opposition groups -- the CDR, the Social Democratic Union (USD) and the National Liberal Alliance (ANL) -- are likely to sign an agreement to supervise the November 3 polls.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Ethnic Gypsies in neighbouring Bulgaria say Ion Cioaba, the self-styled king of Gypsies everywhere, allegedly cheated them by failing to pay $100,000 for 100 tonnes of beans bought from Bulgaria.
- European Union experts will visit Romania to analyse the reasons why some EU member countries do not grant visas to Romanians willing to travel abroad.
LIBERTATEA
- Some 70 percent of Romanian unemployed women refuse the jobs they are offered due to low wages, They often have skills higher than requested. ($=3,271 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
